title: Find All Anagrams in a String
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<int> pCount(26): 26 ints → O(1)
- vector<int> wCount(26): 26 ints → O(1)
- int matches, loop variables: O(1)
- not counted: input strings, returned vector
approach: An anagram of p has identical character frequencies to p. Since only 26 lowercase letters exist, maintain a fixed-size window of length |p| over s, with two frequency arrays of size 26 and a "matches" counter tracking how many letters currently have equal counts in the window and in p. Slide the window one step at a time, updating only the two affected letters and the matches counter in O(1) per step. When matches == 26, the window is an anagram, so record its start index.
hints: An anagram of p shares the exact same per-letter counts as p. With only 26 lowercase letters, what single integer could summarize whether a substring of s matches p's letter profile?

Use a fixed-size sliding window of length |p| over s with two size-26 frequency arrays and a "matches" counter (how many letters have equal counts). For s="cbaebabacd", p="abc": window "cba" gives a=b=c=1, matching p, so index 0 is recorded.

```
build pCount[26] from p
fill wCount[26] for first |p| chars of s
matches = number of i in 0..25 with pCount[i] == wCount[i]
if matches == 26: record 0
for i from |p| to |s|-1:
    remove s[i-|p|] from wCount, update matches
    add s[i] to wCount, update matches
    if matches == 26: record i-|p|+1
```

**p longer than s** - window never fits.
`Input: s = "ab", p = "abc"` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: skipping the `m > n` guard → reads s out of bounds / returns garbage.

**Single character match** - window is one char.
`Input: s = "a", p = "a"` → `Expected: [0]`
⚠️ Bug: forgetting to check the initial window before the loop → returns `[]`.

**All identical characters** - frequency of one letter dominates.
`Input: s = "aaaa", p = "aa"` → `Expected: [0,1,2]`
⚠️ Bug: using a set of characters instead of frequency counts → returns `[]` because set size is 1 for both but counts differ.

**No anagram exists** - matches never reaches 26.
`Input: s = "abcdef", p = "xyz"` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: recording index when `matches > 0` instead of `== 26` → returns `[0,1,2,3,4]`.

followUps.q: What if p and s can contain any Unicode characters, not just lowercase English letters?
followUps.a: Replace the size-26 arrays with hash maps keyed by character, and compare the number of keys whose counts match. The matches counter still works; only the alphabet size grows. TC stays O(n), SC becomes O(k) where k is the number of distinct characters in p.

followUps.q: What if s arrives as an unbounded stream and cannot be stored in memory?
followUps.a: Keep a circular buffer of the last |p| characters and the running frequency map plus matches counter. Emit each matching start index as it is detected. TC remains O(n) amortized, SC is O(|p|) for the buffer and frequency map.

followUps.q: What if you must report substrings that are anagrams of p allowing up to k character substitutions?
followUps.a: Track a "distance" value (e.g., count of letters whose window frequency differs from p, or sum of absolute differences) instead of an exact matches counter. Record a start index whenever the distance is within the allowed budget. TC stays O(n), SC stays O(1) for the fixed alphabet.
